plan: 1 Kings 8:1-11; 2 Chronicles 5:1-14; 1 Kings 8:12-21; 2 Chronicles 6:1-11; 1 Kings 8:22-53; 2 Chronicles 6:12-42

readings.title: The Ark Brought to the Temple
readings.subtitle: The Esteem of YeHoVaH Fills the House
readings.text: [1 Kings 8:1] Then Shelomoh assembled the elders of Yisra’ěl and all the heads of the tribes, the chief fathers of the children of Yisra’ěl, to Sovereign Shelomoh in Yerushalayim, to bring up <dn>את</dn> the ark of the covenant of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> from the City of Daviḏ, which is Tsiyon. [2] And all the men of Yisra’ěl assembled to Sovereign Shelomoh at the festival in the month of Ěythanim, which is the seventh new moon. [3] And all the elders of Yisra’ěl came, and the priests took up <dn>את</dn> the ark, [4] and brought up <dn>את</dn> the ark of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and <dn>את</dn> the Tent of Appointment, and <dn>את</dn> all the set-apart utensils that were in the Tent. And the priests and the Lěvites brought them up, [5] and Sovereign Shelomoh, and all the congregation of Yisra’ěl who had assembled with him, were with him before the ark, slaughtering so many sheep and cattle, that they could not be counted or numbered. [6] And the priests brought in <dn>את</dn> the ark of the covenant of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> to its place, into the Speaking Place of the House, to the Most Set-apart Place, under the wings of the keruḇim, [7] for the keruḇim spread two wings over the place of the ark, and the keruḇim covered over <dn>את</dn> the ark and <dn>את</dn> its poles. [8] And the poles extended so that the ends of the poles were seen from the set-apart place, in front of the Speaking Place, but they were not seen from outside. And they are there to this day. [9] There was naught in the ark, only the two tablets of stone which Mosheh put there at Ḥorěḇ, where <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> made a covenant with the children of Yisra’ěl, when they came out of the land of Mitsrayim. [10] And it came to be, when the priests came out of the Set-apart Place, that the cloud filled <dn>את</dn> the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, [11] so that the priests were unable to stand and perform the service because of the cloud, for the esteem of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> filled <dn>את</dn> the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.

readings.title: Shelomoh's Address
readings.subtitle: YeHoVaH Fulfills His Promise to Daviḏ
readings.text: [1 Kings 8:12] And Shelomoh said, “<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has said <dq><dn>He</dn> would dwell in the dark cloud.</dq> [13] <dn>I</dn> have indeed built <dn>You</dn> an exalted house, an established place for <dn>You</dn> to dwell in forever.” [14] And the sovereign turned around and blessed <dn>את</dn> all the assembly of Yisra’ěl, while all the assembly of Yisra’ěl was standing. [15] And he said, “Blessed be <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl, who spoke with <dn>His</dn> mouth to my father Daviḏ, and with <dn>His</dn> hand has filled it, saying, [16] <dq>Since the day <dn>I</dn> brought <dn>My</dn> people Yisra’ěl out of Mitsrayim, <dn>I</dn> have chosen no city from any tribe of Yisra’ěl in which to build a house for <dn>My</dn> Name to be there, but <dn>I</dn> chose Daviḏ to be over <dn>My</dn> people Yisra’ěl.’</dq> [17] “And it was in the heart of my father Daviḏ to build a house for the Name of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl. [18] “But <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to my father Daviḏ, <dq>‘Because it has been in your heart to build a house for <dn>My</dn> Name, you did well that it was in your heart.</dq> [19] <dq>Only, you do not build the house, but your son, who is coming from your loins, he does build the house for <dn>My</dn> Name.’</dq> [20] “Now <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has established <dn>את</dn> <dn>His</dn> word which <dn>He</dn> spoke, and <dn>I</dn> have been raised up instead of my father Daviḏ, and sit on the throne of Yisra’ěl, as <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> promised, and built a house for the Name of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl, [21] and have appointed there a place for the ark, wherein is the covenant of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> which <dn>He</dn> made with <dn>את</dn> our fathers, when <dn>He</dn> brought them out of the land of Mitsrayim.”

readings.title: Shelomoh's Prayer of Dedication
readings.subtitle: A Plea for Divine Attention
readings.text: [1 Kings 8:22] And Shelomoh stood before the slaughter-place of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> in front of all the assembly of Yisra’ěl, and spread out his hands toward the heavens, [23] and said, “<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl, there is no <dn>Elohim</dn> in the heavens above or on earth below like <dn>You</dn>, guarding <dn>Your</dn> covenant and loving-commitment with <dn>Your</dn> servants who walk before <dn>You</dn> with all their heart, [24] who has guarded <dn>את</dn> that which <dn>You</dn> did promise <dn>Your</dn> servant Daviḏ <dn>my</dn> father. Indeed, <dn>You</dn> have both spoken with <dn>Your</dn> mouth and have filled it with <dn>Your</dn> hand, as it is this day. [25] “And now, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl, guard <dn>את</dn> what <dn>You</dn> promised <dn>Your</dn> servant Daviḏ <dn>my</dn> father, saying, <dq>‘There is not to cease a man of yours before <dn>Me</dn>, sitting on the throne of Yisra’ěl – only, if your sons guard their way, to walk before <dn>Me</dn> as you have walked before <dn>Me</dn>.’</dq> [26] “And now, O <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl, please let <dn>Your</dn> word come true which <dn>You</dn> have spoken to <dn>Your</dn> servant Daviḏ <dn>my</dn> father. [27] “For is it true: <dn>Elohim</dn> dwells on the earth? See, the heavens and the heavens of the heavens are unable to contain <dn>You</dn>, how much less this House which <dn>I</dn> have built! [28] “Yet, shall <dn>You</dn> turn to the prayer of <dn>Your</dn> servant and his supplication, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>my</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn>, and listen to the cry and the prayer which <dn>Your</dn> servant is praying before <dn>You</dn> today? [29] “For <dn>Your</dn> eyes to be open toward this House night and day, toward the place of which <dn>You</dn> said, <dq>‘<dn>My</dn> Name is there,’</dq> to listen to the prayer which <dn>Your</dn> servant makes toward this place. [30] “Then, shall <dn>You</dn> hear the supplication of <dn>Your</dn> servant and of <dn>Your</dn> people Yisra’ěl when they pray toward this place, when <dn>You</dn> hear in <dn>Your</dn> dwelling place, in the heavens? And shall <dn>You</dn> hear, and forgive?

readings.title: Petitions for Yisra’ěl
readings.subtitle: Forgiveness and Restoration
readings.text: [1 Kings 8:31] “If anyone sins against his neighbour, and he has lifted up an oath on him, to cause him to swear, and comes and swears before <dn>Your</dn> slaughter-place in this House, [32] then hear in the heavens, and act and rightly rule <dn>Your</dn> servants, declaring the wrongdoer wrong, bringing his way on his head, and declaring the righteous right by giving him according to his righteousness. [33] “When <dn>Your</dn> people Yisra’ěl are smitten before an enemy, because they have sinned against <dn>You</dn>, and they shall turn back to <dn>You</dn> and confess <dn>Your</dn> Name, and pray and make supplication to <dn>You</dn> in this House, [34] then hear in the heavens, and forgive <dn>את</dn> the sin of <dn>Your</dn> people Yisra’ěl, and bring them back to the land which <dn>You</dn> gave to their fathers. [35] “When the heavens are shut up and there is no rain because they sin against <dn>You</dn>, when they pray toward this place and confess <dn>Your</dn> Name, and turn from their sin because <dn>You</dn> afflict them, [36] then hear in the heavens, and forgive <dn>את</dn> the sin of <dn>Your</dn> servants, <dn>Your</dn> people Yisra’ěl – for <dn>You</dn> teach them <dn>את</dn> the good way in which they should walk – and shall give rain on <dn>Your</dn> land which <dn>You</dn> have given to <dn>Your</dn> people as an inheritance. [37] “When there is scarcity of food in the land; when there is pestilence, blight, mildew, locusts, grasshoppers; when their enemy distresses them in the land of their cities; any plague, any sickness, [38] whatever prayer, whatever supplication made by anyone of all <dn>Your</dn> people Yisra’ěl, each knowing the plague of his own heart, and shall spread out his hands toward this House, [39] then hear in the heavens, <dn>Your</dn> dwelling place, and forgive, and act, and render unto everyone according to all his ways, whose heart <dn>You</dn> know. Because <dn>You</dn> – <dn>You</dn> alone – know <dn>את</dn> the hearts of all the sons of men, [40] so that they fear <dn>You</dn> all the days that they live in the land which <dn>You</dn> gave to our fathers.

readings.title: Petitions for Foreigners and Captives
readings.subtitle: A People Set Apart
readings.text: [1 Kings 8:41] “Also, concerning a foreigner, who is not of <dn>Your</dn> people Yisra’ěl, but has come from a far land for <dn>Your</dn> Name’s sake – [42] since they hear of <dn>Your</dn> great Name and <dn>Your</dn> strong hand and <dn>Your</dn> outstretched arm – and he shall come and pray toward this House, [43] hear in the heavens <dn>Your</dn> dwelling place, and do <dn>את</dn> according to all for which the foreigner calls to <dn>You</dn>, so that all peoples of the earth know <dn>את</dn> <dn>Your</dn> Name and fear <dn>You</dn>, as do <dn>Your</dn> people Yisra’ěl, and know that this House which <dn>I</dn> have built is called by <dn>Your</dn> Name. [44] “When <dn>Your</dn> people go out to battle against their enemy, in the way that <dn>You</dn> send them, and they shall pray to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> toward the city which <dn>You</dn> have chosen and toward the House which <dn>I</dn> have built for <dn>Your</dn> Name, [45] then shall <dn>You</dn> hear in the heavens their prayer and their supplication, and maintain <dn>את</dn> their cause? [46] “When they sin against <dn>You</dn> – for there is no one who does not sin – and <dn>You</dn> become enraged with them and give them to the enemy, and they take them captive to the land of the enemy, far or near; [47] and they shall turn back unto their heart in the land where they have been taken captive, and shall turn, and make supplication to <dn>You</dn> in the land of those who took them captive, saying, ‘We have sinned and acted crookedly, we have committed wrong,’ [48] and they shall turn back to <dn>You</dn> with all their heart and with all their being in the land of their enemies who led them away captive, and shall pray to <dn>You</dn> toward their land which <dn>You</dn> gave to their fathers, the city which <dn>You</dn> have chosen and the House which <dn>I</dn> have built for <dn>Your</dn> Name, [49] then shall <dn>You</dn> hear in the heavens <dn>Your</dn> dwelling place their prayer and their supplication, and maintain <dn>את</dn> their cause, [50] and forgive <dn>Your</dn> people who have sinned against <dn>You</dn>, and <dn>את</dn> all their transgressions which they have transgressed against <dn>You</dn>? And give them compassion before those who took them captive, and they shall have compassion on them. [51] For they are <dn>Your</dn> people and <dn>Your</dn> inheritance, whom <dn>You</dn> brought out of Mitsrayim, out of the iron furnace. [52] “Let <dn>Your</dn> eyes be open to the supplication of <dn>Your</dn> servant and the supplication of <dn>Your</dn> people Yisra’ěl, to listen to them whenever they call to <dn>You</dn>. [53] “For <dn>You</dn> have separated them unto <dn>Yourself</dn> for an inheritance, out of all the peoples of the earth, as <dn>You</dn> spoke by the hand of <dn>Your</dn> servant Mosheh, when <dn>You</dn> brought our fathers out of Mitsrayim, O Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.”
